turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_target_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_target_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have a yield strength CLOSEST to 1051 MPa — not the highest, the closest to that value — then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

**Step 1 – Understand the target.**
The target value we must approach (1051 MPa) lies far above the bulk of the training distribution (which mostly ranges 150–700 MPa), with only a handful of outliers reaching ~700–900 MPa. Since no training sample reaches 1051 MPa, the "closest" candidates will be those predicted to have the *highest* strength, i.e., those most similar in composition/processing to the highest-strength training samples.

**Step 2 – Identify what drives high strength in training data.**
Sorting training samples by `target`, the top values (908, 899, 864, 772, 738, 734, 726, 722, 709, 686, 685, 680 MPa …) are overwhelmingly:
- `heat_treatment = quench_temper`
- `route = wrought` (dominant among the top group)
- Moderate Cr (≈5–14 wt%), moderate Ni (≈5–15 wt%), Co present (≈2–10 wt%), Mo modest (≈1–3 wt%), C moderate (≈0.2–0.7 wt%)
- Solutionizing temp fairly high (1050–1230 °C), aging temp 480–650 °C, cooling rate moderate/variable (not necessarily extreme).

Averaging the top wrought/quench_temper training rows gives an approximate "high-strength centroid":
Cr≈8.1, Ni≈8.5, Co≈5.5, Mo≈2.0, C≈0.33 (with sol_temp ~1150–1200 °C, aging ~500–650 °C).

**Step 3 – Score pool candidates.**
Restricting to `quench_temper` + `wrought` candidates (matching the dominant high-strength group) and computing a squared-distance metric to the centroid (Cr, Ni, Co, Mo, C):

| candidate | Cr | Ni | Co | Mo | C | distance² |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c099 | 8.48 | 8.20 | 6.27 | 1.91 | 0.42 | 0.85 (best) |
| c082 | 6.47 | 9.45 | 6.34 | 2.09 | 0.53 | 4.2 |
| c049 | 9.54 | 11.17 | 5.60 | 2.04 | 0.58 | 9.5 |
| c069 | 7.52 | 12.70 | 7.01 | 1.89 | 0.47 | 20.4 |
| c052 | 5.64 | 12.30 | 6.43 | 1.88 | 0.70 | 21.5 |
| c085 | 11.93 | 12.52 | 6.20 | 1.88 | 0.54 | 31.7 |
| c037 | 9.53 | 14.23 | 6.24 | 2.57 | 0.27 | 36.0 |

Other quench_temper/wrought candidates (c007, c009, c013, c017, c035, c038, c039, c045, c046, c051, c058, c059, c073, c075, c078, c097, c098) deviate strongly on at least one key element (e.g., Ni≈0, Co≈0, Cr extreme, Co=15, etc.), making them poorer matches to the high-strength profile.

**Step 4 – Select top 5.**
The five candidates whose compositions and processing parameters most closely resemble the highest-strength training alloys (and thus are predicted to be closest to 1051 MPa) are:

Final: c099, c082, c049, c069, c052
